RED-FLAGS REPORT: PRAIRIE AEROSTRUCTURES HOLDINGS DILIGENCE REVIEW
Date: [Current Review Date]
Matter: Diligence Review – Prairie Aerostructures Holdings
Subject: Critical Issues Identified in Counterparty Markup and Disclosure Schedules

_______________________________________________________________________________

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

This red-flags report identifies five critical issues in the Prairie Aerostructures Holdings transaction that require immediate attention and negotiation. The counterparty's latest markup introduces significant deviations from firm-standard provisions, coupled with scheduled disclosures that heighten risk exposure. Per the latest partner instruction, any survival-period reduction constitutes a walk-away issue and is flagged with highest priority.

_______________________________________________________________________________

1. SURVIVAL PERIOD REDUCTION — WALK-AWAY ISSUE [PRIORITY: CRITICAL]

RED FLAG: The counterparty markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens survival for core representations below market standard.

ISSUE DETAIL:
• The markup reduces the survival period for fundamental representations (e.g., organization, authority, capitalization, title to assets)
• This directly contradicts Exhibit B, which sets a longer survival matrix for core representations
• Per latest partner correspondence, the client treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue
• The markup provision creates ambiguity against the existing survival matrix and introduces counterparty favorable reductions

BUSINESS IMPACT: 
Reduced survival periods compress the client's remedies window for post-closing discovery of breaches. This is incompatible with client risk tolerance and M&A market practice for transactions of this scope.

RECOMMENDATION:
Reject the survival-period reduction outright. Insist on Exhibit B terms as the governing survival matrix. If counterparty will not concede, recommend deal termination per client's stated walk-away position.

_______________________________________________________________________________

2. INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCTION & BASKET CONVERSION [PRIORITY: HIGH]

RED FLAG: The counterparty markup silently reduces the indemnification cap and converts the basket from a deductible structure to a tipping basket.

ISSUE DETAIL:
• The cap reduction is not clearly identified in the markup but appears in comparison to firm precedent
• The basket conversion changes the mechanics fundamentally: a deductible (all losses aggregate from dollar one) becomes a tipping basket (losses accrue until threshold, then all losses including those below threshold are recoverable)
• This conversion is materially favorable to the seller and increases client exposure
• Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that this markup change would silently shift to the buyer's indemnification burden

BUSINESS IMPACT:
The combined effect of cap reduction and basket conversion significantly erodes the indemnification recovery available to the buyer. The tipping-basket structure penalizes the client for smaller, repeated breaches and increases aggregate exposure.

RECOMMENDATION:
(a) Restore the original indemnification cap
(b) Reject the basket conversion and reinstate the deductible structure
(c) Cross-reference Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities against the indemnification scope to ensure no unintended shifts in liability allocation

_______________________________________________________________________________

3. MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION [PRIORITY: HIGH]

RED FLAG: The counterparty markup adds new carve-outs to the Material Adverse Effect definition, specifically excluding regulatory actions of the type currently pending against the target.

ISSUE DETAIL:
• The markup introduces MAE carve-outs for "regulatory action" without limiting scope or temporal bounds
• Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that directly intersect these carve-outs
• The carve-outs are newly inserted by counterparty, not in firm-standard precedent
• The timing of these additions suggests awareness of the Schedule 3.7 disclosures and intent to limit buyer remedies

BUSINESS IMPACT:
If regulatory actions progress during the transaction period or post-closing, the buyer will be unable to invoke MAE protections. The pending inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7 create acute risk that regulatory outcomes will occur after closing but fall outside the buyer's remedy window.

RECOMMENDATION:
(a) Delete the regulatory action carve-outs or substantially narrow their scope (e.g., apply only to general regulatory changes of industry-wide application, not entity-specific actions)
(b) If counterparty insists on any regulatory carve-out, tie it temporally: exclude only regulatory actions not reasonably foreseeable as of the signing date
(c) Request detailed status updates on the two pending inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7 and obtain counterparty representations regarding anticipated timeline and exposure
(d) Consider survival period extensions for representations related to regulatory compliance (this aligns with the client's walk-away position on general survival reductions and is responsive to specific regulatory risk)

_______________________________________________________________________________

4. CONFLICTING INDEMNIFICATION SCOPE & SCHEDULE 5.2 RETAINED LIABILITIES [PRIORITY: HIGH]

RED FLAG: Schedule 5.2 discloses retained liabilities, but the counterparty markup's indemnification changes create ambiguity about which party bears these liabilities post-closing.

ISSUE DETAIL:
• Schedule 5.2 explicitly lists liabilities the seller retains post-closing
• The markup's indemnification cap reduction and basket conversion do not explicitly exclude these scheduled items
• The interaction between retained liabilities (Schedule 5.2) and indemnification scope (markup language) is unresolved
• Risk: the buyer could be required to indemnify seller for liabilities the seller explicitly retained

BUSINESS IMPACT:
The buyer faces double-exposure: paying retained liabilities directly through purchase price allocation, while potentially being forced to indemnify seller for breach-of-warranty claims arising from those same liabilities.

RECOMMENDATION:
(a) Explicitly carve out Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities from all indemnification obligations
(b) Confirm in indemnification definitions that "breach" of representations regarding liabilities does not include liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2
(c) Add a side-letter or amendment clarifying the seller retains all liability for Schedule 5.2 items regardless of post-closing discovery

_______________________________________________________________________________

5. SCHEDULED REGULATORY INQUIRIES — DISCLOSURE & RISK ASSESSMENT [PRIORITY: MEDIUM-HIGH]

RED FLAG: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries; the timing, scope, and potential outcomes are underspecified.

ISSUE DETAIL:
• Two regulatory inquiries are pending but details regarding the inquiries are sparse in the available disclosure schedules
• The inquiries fall squarely within the regulatory action carve-outs the counterparty added to the MAE definition (Red Flag #3)
• No information provided regarding counterparty's assessment of exposure, timeline, or likelihood of enforcement action
• No indemnification carve-out or survival extension addresses post-closing resolution of these inquiries

BUSINESS IMPACT:
If regulatory inquiries mature into enforcement actions post-closing, the buyer will have no recourse because:
1. The regulatory action is carved out of MAE (Red Flag #3)
2. Survival periods may be too short to pursue indemnification claims (Red Flag #1)
3. The scope of retained liabilities (Schedule 5.2) may absorb these costs

RECOMMENDATION:
(a) Request comprehensive disclosure regarding each pending regulatory inquiry: agency, subject matter, timeline, estimated exposure, and counterparty's internal assessment
(b) Demand that counterparty represent that it has disclosed all material regulatory communications, inquiries, and investigations
(c) Negotiate a carve-out from the regulatory action MAE exception for these two specifically identified inquiries, with a survival period of 24-36 months for representations related to regulatory compliance
(d) Consider an escrow holdback or earnout provision tied to regulatory outcomes for 18-24 months post-closing
(e) Obtain counterparty's insurance certificates and loss-run history related to regulatory matters

_______________________________________________________________________________

SUMMARY TABLE OF RED FLAGS

| Priority | Issue | Red Flag | Action |
|----------|-------|----------|--------|
| CRITICAL | Survival Period Reduction | Contradicts Exhibit B; conflicts with client walk-away position | REJECT; walk away if unresolved |
| HIGH | Indemnification Cap & Basket | Silent reduction + tipping basket conversion | Restore original cap; reinstate deductible |
| HIGH | MAE Regulatory Carve-outs | Excludes pending Schedule 3.7 inquiries | Delete or narrow substantially |
| HIGH | Schedule 5.2 / Indemnification Conflict | Retained liabilities exposure | Explicit carve-out from indemnification |
| MED-HIGH | Schedule 3.7 Regulatory Inquiries | Underspecified disclosures; acute post-closing risk | Request detailed disclosure; extend survival |

_______________________________________________________________________________

INTEGRATION WITH CLIENT INSTRUCTION

Per the latest partner correspondence, the client will concede the basket conversion (Red Flag #2, item 2b) but insists that any survival-period reduction (Red Flag #1) is non-negotiable and constitutes a walk-away issue.

This analysis respects that priority ordering: Red Flag #1 is flagged as CRITICAL with a walk-away recommendation, while the basket conversion concession is noted as a potential negotiation point. All other issues remain full-priority red flags requiring resolution before closing.

_______________________________________________________________________________

NEXT STEPS

1. Reject survival-period reduction; confirm client's walk-away position with counterparty
2. Demand revised markup resolving Red Flag #1 (survival), Red Flag #3 (MAE carve-outs), and Red Flag #4 (Schedule 5.2 carve-out)
3. Request detailed Schedule 3.7 regulatory disclosure (Red Flag #5)
4. Negotiate resolution of indemnification cap and consider concession on basket conversion only (Red Flag #2)
5. If counterparty will not move materially on Red Flag #1, recommend termination

_______________________________________________________________________________

This report is prepared for the private use of the client and engaged counsel. It contains analysis of legal risks specific to this transaction and reflects the current markup and disclosure status as of the review date.
